plan: This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price sealed-bid auction: the winner pays the second-highest bid, and bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy. Bidding exactly my value ensures I win whenever my value exceeds others' bids (profitable), and I never overpay since the price is set by the second-highest bid, not my own. There's no incentive to shade or inflate my bid.

This auction structure is equivalent to a second-price (Vickrey) auction, since the winner pays the second-highest bid amount. In such auctions, bidding one's true value is the dominant strategy regardless of what others bid - it maximizes expected profit. Bidding higher than value risks winning at a loss; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I should bid exactly my true value of $20.

This is effectively a second-price sealed-bid auction (via the ascending clock mechanism), where the winner pays the second-highest bid. In such auctions, bidding your true value is the dominant strategy: it maximizes expected profit regardless of others' bids, since you win whenever your value exceeds the second-highest bid, and pay less than your value, ensuring non-negative profit. Bidding higher risks overpaying; bidding lower risks losing profitable opportunities. Therefore, I will bid exactly my true value of $20.
